newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs seen underperforming Bunds after rise.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs seen underperforming Bunds after rise.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds (OLOs) should underperform Bunds in the near term after a two-day rally that has taken many by surprise, dealers said.
But few were betting on a sell off.

The rally, spurred by tame U.S. inflation data, on Tuesday took the yield on the benchmark 6.25 percent OLO 26, maturing in March 2007, down to 5.81 percent, just four basis points over equivalent Bunds. Two days ago the spread was 14 basis points.
"We think that OLOs will underperform now against Bunds for the rest of the week, but it's not certain," a Luxembourg-based trader said.
"It's quite a spread narrowing but we don't see any sellers in the market for the moment...I would not sell Belgium vs Germany for now," a trader at a foreign primary dealer in Brussels said.

Belgian traders noted only the 10-year OLO 26 was still trading over Bunds. Five year paper was around 10 basis points below German Bobls, while Belgium's 20-year bond was around seven basis points under, one said.
Few expected the 10-year OLOs to follow France, and trade through Bunds. "I doubt it. We're going to have problems just holding flat," one said.
Another dealer forecast that five-year paper was more likely to get cheaper, flattening the shape of the five-to-ten year part of the yield curve.
"Five years are looking very expensive against 10-years," he said. "In general we think (the market's) getting a little bit ridiculous. We have to be cautious."
